constructions.title: Rows of the CTD extract per value of its unit column

ctd.categorical.Enhed.*.is: Rows of `data/raw/oda/ctd.csv.gz` carrying this exact string in the `Enhed` column, counted over every row; blank and differently spelled values are their own keys.

constructions.what: How many rows of the CTD extract carry each unit string, for the unit column that stays under the cardinality cap and so is kept whole.
constructions.model: `scan()` in `scripts/enums.py` reads every row with `csv.DictReader` in `latin-1` and adds one to a `collections.Counter` per column and value (`c[v] += 1`); a column that passes `CARD_CAP` distinct values is dropped to a numeric sample. `main()` writes the surviving counters as `rec["categorical"][col]`, most common first.
assumptions: One row of the extract is one measurement of one parameter at one depth.

justified.text: The counter is incremented once per row and column for the value found there, so a unit's count is exactly the rows written in that unit.
The counts are written unaltered, keyed by the value as a string.

gaps: The unit is counted per row without the parameter on the same row: which parameter carries which unit is not stored, and can only be read off by matching totals.
A unit written two ways counts as two units.
void_if: the CTD extract is refetched and `enums.py` is not rerun
constructions.licenses: How many rows of the extract carry each unit string, and so which parameter totals a unit total can match.
constructions.not_licensed: That a given row's parameter is in a given unit.

confirmed.by: agent w3-dz (written against the code it describes: scan() and main() in enums.py, the Counter increment and the categorical write; 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)

constructions.title: Agreement between random connected partitions of the station graph

graphs.*.stations.is: Stations in the graph: those measured on every panel variable in at least `MIN_MONTHS` months and with a position, the first `MAX_STATIONS` of them; for the graphs named `water` and `knn_same_area`, only those inside the coastline file's extent.

graphs.*.contiguous_null_ari.is: The mean adjusted Rand index over every pair of the random connected partitions `contiguous_null` draws on this graph with the seeds `101`, `202`, `303` and `404`, their group sizes matched to the official water bodies' sizes scaled to the graph.

constructions.what: How far two partitions of the station graph agree from contiguity alone: the floor any contiguous derived partition must beat.
constructions.model: `contiguous_null(adj, sizes, seed)` picks a free station at random and grows a group by breadth-first accretion until its size is met, for each size in turn, leftovers becoming singletons. `main()` draws one partition per seed, computes `ari` from `partition_stability.py` for each pair, and stores `null_floor = sum(nn) / len(nn)` rounded to three places.
assumptions: The official water bodies' size distribution is a fair size distribution for random partitions of the same stations.

justified.text: The partitions are connected by construction: each group grows only along graph edges from its seed.
The stored value is the mean over the pairs of null partitions, written with the graph's station count.

gaps: The seeds are fixed, so the value is a mean over the pairs of one set of `4` partitions: a sample of the null, with no spread stored.
The graph holds only the stations measured on every variable, capped at `MAX_STATIONS`, not the whole panel.
void_if: the panel or the station overlay changes and `partition_contiguous.py` is not rerun
constructions.licenses: That contiguity alone makes partitions of these stations agree above the chance level the adjusted Rand index corrects for.
constructions.not_licensed: The null distribution's spread, or anything about effort fields or c-squares.

confirmed.by: agent w3-dz (written against the code it describes: contiguous_null() and the null_floor loop in partition_contiguous.py main(), MIN_MONTHS, MAX_STATIONS and ari() in partition_stability.py; 2026-09-11; not yet read by the project owner)
